title: Our first full day together
arrival: Choose a comfortable seat. Have a pencil ready. Notice something interesting in our room.
note: Flexible first-day template. Confirm the teaching date before saving a dated copy. Students may finish all three conversation decks within one hour. Move on when the purpose is met; carry unfinished activities into another day.

blocks.title: Welcome and practise the essentials
blocks.notes: Briefly practise our attention signal, safe walking, listening, respectful language, asking for help and caring for materials. Say: We will practise how our classroom works as we do things together. Comfortable friendship seating is fine today; intervene for exclusion, crowding, access or disruption. Try different groupings during activities.

blocks.title: Talk, move, connect
blocks.notes: Find Someone Similar → Find Someone Different → Would You Rather. Think, move safely, find a partner, ask the follow-up, listen. A seated partner route and passing are welcome. Change partners; include someone who is waiting. Allow up to about an hour for all three decks together, and move faster when the class is ready.

blocks.title: Build our classroom community
blocks.notes: Discuss what makes our room safe, fair and welcoming. Show Whole Class Responsibilities, then Team Captain Responsibilities. Everyone helps; captains lead through service. Practise one cleanup task. Briefly show Morning Screen, lessons, Student Hub and Games & Activities (5–10 minutes).

blocks.title: Discovery Booklets / Werewolf training
blocks.notes: Finish worthwhile Discovery work without requiring private disclosures. Early finishers clarify an idea or design a welcoming classroom. If time remains, teach Werewolf roles, night/day order, voting and a coached demonstration. Otherwise start the game lesson after lunch.

blocks.title: Quiet reading
blocks.notes: Settle and read for 20–30 minutes. Have books available; offer a comfortable reading position. Model the daily after-lunch reading routine.

blocks.title: Werewolf: learn, practise, play
blocks.notes: Allow about 45–60 minutes. Open the existing dedicated ELA lesson. Use the owned Ultimate Werewolf deck and the established 25-player setup, checking exact abilities on physical cards. Model one atmospheric story sentence without inventing evidence about players. Departed players listen and track the story. End with one strength in listening or storytelling and one next step.

blocks.title: Care for our classroom
blocks.notes: Everyone restores their workstation and shared materials, sorts waste and stacks chairs safely. Captains coordinate shelves, cushions, dropped supplies, sweeping, compost, tables and fair seating turns. Captains give kind reminders and call the supervising adult for safety concerns.

blocks.title: Outside: Capture the Flag
blocks.notes: Teacher checks the play area and identifies boundaries, a stop signal, two equal teams and safe flag zones. Use gentle tagging only; no grabbing or guarding bodies. Tagged players walk back to their own side before rejoining. No physical contact to take a flag. Offer an accessible walking role or boundary/helper role. Explain how a flag is returned and stop for a quick demonstration before play. End with time to gather equipment and dismiss calmly.

backups: Choose another conversation card and a new partner.
Name-memory challenge: in groups of four, say your name and an interest; each person recalls a partner’s interest. Passing is welcome.
Draw a great Grade 6 classroom. Label three features that help people belong and explain one to a partner.
Rehearse a 30-second Werewolf opening with a partner: setting, sound, change. Give one helpful comment.
Continue Discovery Booklets, read a little longer or extend outdoor activity when practical.
